report:
Weekly Purchasing & Demand Review

Operational Context & Demand Shift
Store replenishment requests over the past two weeks show a pronounced divergence in category dynamics across all four districts (HK Island, Kowloon, NT East, and NT West). Store orders are shifting heavily into refreshing, water-based treats and fruit flavours, while chocolate-coated confections continue to soften.

Key Findings
1. Water-based Surge:
Store requests for water-based items exceeded baseline expectations by +37.4% over the past 14 days (85,408 requested units vs 62,159 expected), accelerating to +56.9% in the last 7 days. The estimated sustained cohort uplift is +34.7% (80% CI: +33.7% to +35.7%). Heavy demand resulted in 10,624 unfulfilled units at the central warehouse (fill rate of 87.6%).
Within this category, strawberry flavours were the primary volume driver, led by Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar (+4,140 excess units) and Strawberry Breeze Ice Bar (+3,325 excess units), alongside strong gains in Watermelon Chill Bar (+1,507 excess units) and Coconut Water Ice Bar (+1,342 excess units).

2. Network-Wide Strawberry Flavour Uplift:
Strawberry items across all formats saw request share rise from 23.4% expected to 27.3% actual, sustained across all 20 stores. Over the last 14 days, strawberry items recorded +39.6% excess demand (50,182 requested units vs 35,941 expected), with fulfillment dropping to 84.7% (7,684 unfulfilled units).

3. Softening in Chocolate-Coated Products:
Store replenishment requests for chocolate-coated items fell -11.1% below expectations over the past 14 days (share dropping to 12.7% vs 16.7% expected). The decline was concentrated in standard and value-priced chocolate items (estimated sustained cohort effect of -11.7%, 80% CI: -13.3% to -10.1%), led by Coffee Crunch Bar (-684 excess units) and White Choc Raspberry Bar (-441 excess units). Chocolate-coated: three-product group items experienced a milder decline of -3.4%.

4. Non-Coated Dairy Performance:
Mid-calorie dairy items without chocolate coating maintained healthy momentum (+10.1% estimated sustained effect, +164 cases), led by Mango Sticky Rice Bar and Red Bean Ice Bar. Other non-coated dairy lines (including family tubs and gelato cups) remained steady (+3.7% sustained effect, +43 cases).

Warehouse Capacity & Purchasing Recommendations
The planned purchase modifications adjust demand assumptions to reflect observed sustained shifts while respecting physical storage limits:
- Increase Water-based products by +599 cases (+10.07 pallets footprint). This priority adjustment captures high demand and protects an estimated $81,393 in lost margin.
- Increase Mid-calorie non-coated dairy by +164 cases (+3.02 pallets footprint).
- Increase Other non-coated dairy by +43 cases (+0.70 pallets footprint).
- Reduce The seven-product coated group by -68 cases (-1.41 pallets footprint).
- Reduce Chocolate-coated: three-product group items by -6 cases (-0.10 pallets footprint).

Whole-warehouse peak capacity occupancy is projected at 51.5 pallets against a maximum limit of 71.0 pallets (inherited peak pallets also at 51.5). The purchase plan fits physical storage capacity with 0 excess pallets.

presentation.title: Water-based and strawberry treats surge above forecast while chocolate-coated items soften
presentation.html:
Main observations

All Districts · 25 SKUs

Water-based

+34.7% sustained cohort effect (CI: +33.7% to +35.7%)

Replenishment requests exceeded forecast by +37.4% over the past 14 days (85,408 units requested vs 62,159 expected), climbing to +56.9% in the most recent week. High request pressure led to 10,624 unfulfilled units (87.6% fulfillment rate).

Network-wide · 14 SKUs

Strawberry flavour

+39.6% 14-day request deviation (+61.3% last 7d)

Strawberry share expanded from 23.4% expected to 27.3% actual across all 20 stores. Unfilled demand reached 7,684 units as store ordering outran warehouse deliveries (84.7% fill rate), led by Strawberry Orchard and Strawberry Breeze ice bars.

All Districts · 10 SKUs

Chocolate-coated

-11.1% 14-day request deviation (share: 12.7% vs 16.7%)

Persistent softening across all 20 stores over 17 running days. The decline is concentrated in the larger seven-product coated group (-11.7% estimated sustained effect), while the three-product coated group experienced only a modest softening (-3.4%).

Softening across 20 stores

Demand is rotating noticeably from rich chocolate-coated confections into refreshing water-based and fruit lines, led specifically by strawberry ice bars. With fulfillment falling below 88% on surge items, purchasing quantities must expand to prevent recurring warehouse stockouts.

Secondary observations

Non-Water-based · 24 SKUs

Mid calorie dairy

+10.1% sustained cohort effect (CI: +9.1% to +11.2%)

Steady positive deviation across non-coated dairy items (Mango Sticky Rice Bar, Milk Tea Bar, Red Bean Ice Bar), avoiding the downturn seen in chocolate lines.

+164 cases planned
Non-Water-based · 16 SKUs

Other non-chocolate dairy

+3.7% sustained cohort effect (CI: +2.4% to +5.1%)

Stable performance overall across tubs and premium gelato, resulting in a gentle increase of +43 cases across 16 SKUs with minimal pallet footprint impact.

+43 cases planned

Action recommendations

Action Group / Scope Adjustment Detail Rationale
Increase Water-based (25 SKUs) +599 cases (+10.07 pallets footprint) Replenishment requests running +37.4% above expectation; avoids an estimated $81,393 in lost margin.
Increase Mid calorie dairy (24 SKUs) +164 cases (+3.02 pallets footprint) Sustained +10.1% lift in demand across non-chocolate snacks and mochi lines.
Increase Other non-coated dairy (16 SKUs) +43 cases (+0.70 pallets footprint) Mild +3.7% sustained gain across family tubs and gelato cups.
Reduce Chocolate-coated: seven-product group (7 SKUs) -68 cases (-1.41 pallets footprint) Sustained -11.7% softening across cones and crunch bars; reallocates stock room.
Reduce Chocolate-coated: three-product group (3 SKUs) -6 cases (-0.10 pallets footprint) Minor -3.4% softening in premium chocolate bars; slight order trimming.
Warehouse Capacity Check: Total warehouse peak occupancy with all cohort adjustments is projected at 51.5 pallets against the 71.0 pallet physical capacity limit. The proposed buying plan fits warehouse capacity with 0 excess pallets.

claims.text: Water-based frozen treats experienced an estimated sustained uplift of 34.7% (80% CI: 33.7% to 35.7%) relative to baseline expectations, with raw recent 14-day requests exceeding forecast by 37.4% (85408 requested units vs 62159 expected).

Strawberry flavour products saw persistent demand growth across all 20 stores in all four districts, with request share reaching 27.3% vs 23.4% expected and daily requested units reaching 50182 vs 35941 expected (39.6% deviation over 14 days, accelerating to 61.3% over the last 7 days).

The primary drivers within water-based products are strawberry-flavoured ice bars, led by Strawberry Orchard Ice Bar (4140 excess units), Strawberry Breeze Ice Bar (3325 excess units), and Strawberry Burst Bar (2188 excess units).

Operational fulfillment for Strawberry flavour dropped to 84.7% (7684 unfilled units out of 50182 requested), while total Water-based fulfillment reached 87.6% (10624 unfilled units out of 85408 requested), indicating significant warehouse-level stock pressure.

Chocolate-coated products softened persistently across all 20 stores, with actual share falling to 13.2% vs 16.8% expected (-11.1% recent 14-day deviation); the seven-product cohort within this category showed an estimated sustained effect of -11.7% (80% CI: -13.3% to -10.1%).

The three-product higher-price-per-100-ml coated group exhibited a mild softening of -3.4% estimated sustained effect (80% CI: -5.8% to -0.9%), with computed buying recommendations 6 cases below the unadjusted plan.

Dairy-based non-chocolate items saw modest growth: mid-calorie dairy items showed an estimated sustained uplift of 10.1% (164 cases), while low/high-calorie non-chocolate dairy items increased by 3.7% (43 cases).

Purchasing allocations increase Water-based orders by 599 cases (10.07 pallets footprint), increase Mid-calorie dairy by 164 cases (3.02 pallets), and reduce the seven-product Chocolate-coated cohort by -68 cases (-1.41 pallets), while whole-warehouse peak capacity remains at 51.5 pallets against a 71.0 pallet limit (fits physical capacity with 0 excess pallets).

questions.text: Did recent convenience store promotions or district-level retail displays specifically feature strawberry ice bars over the past two weeks?
Are stores reporting physical cabinet space reallocation away from chocolate-coated cones in favour of water ice bars?

sample.rule: At least 3 products, 7 observed days, 100 requested units and 95% expected-row coverage; this is an adequacy heuristic.

result.prior_year_basis: Same calendar dates one year earlier, same products and districts; not weather-adjusted.

shift_share.basis: Equal-length requested-unit windows; arithmetic decomposition, not evidence of individual customer switching.

result.warehouse_scope: Supplier receipts and expected arrivals cover shared warehouse products; they are not district-specific stock.

editorial_review.feedback:
Editorial review of the first draft: the weather-adjusted residual was incorrectly
explained by hot weather, two headline blocks repeated one another, two different cohort scopes
were combined under a dairy-tub label, and +43 cases were called Hold. Re-author the report from
the current evidence. Keep a single host-owned title, one informative comparison per card, and
the exact group definitions. Show each distinct observation separately. Use operational queries
when you need evidence for an explanation; ask about missing context rather than assert it.
Keep the plain-text report concise. These are editorial corrections, not an instruction to find
any particular trend or make the policy outperform the rule.
editorial_review.method: Real Gemini regeneration; no manually edited report text.
human_followup: Corrected per-item price-tier labels that had been inferred from a per-100-ml split, using the exact seven-product/three-product cohort scopes instead.
Removed the two repeated fulfillment footer statistics. Original Gemini output is retained in the reviewed-report artifact.
Clarified that the six-case reduction is a computed purchase adjustment, not a raw request change; bound each related cohort/fulfillment/share source to its existing card magnifier.
